sentences.zh: 列傳第六十八 列女 ○阿鄰妻 李寶信妻 韓慶民妻 雷婦師氏 康住住 李文妻 李英妻 相琪妻 阿魯真 撒合輦妻 許古妻 馮妙真 蒲察氏 烏古論氏 素蘭妻 忙哥妻 尹氏 白氏 聶孝女 仲德妻 寶符李氏 張鳳奴

translations.literal: Biographies 68 — Exemplary Women — the Wife of A Lin; the Wife of Li Baoxin; the Wife of Han Qingmin; Mrs. Shi of the Lei Family; Kang Zhuzhu; the Wife of Li Wen; the Wife of Li Ying; the Wife of Xiang Qi; A Luzhen; the Wife of Sahe Nian; the Wife of Xu Gu; Feng Miaozhen; the Pucha Clan; the Wugulun Clan; the Wife of Su Lan; the Wife of Mang Ge; Lady Yin; Lady Bai; Nie the Filial Daughter; the Wife of Zhongde; Lady Li of Baofu; Zhang Fengnu
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 68 — Exemplary Women — including the Wife of A Lin, Li Baoxin's wife, Han Qingmin's wife, Mrs. Shi of the Lei household, Kang Zhuzhu, Li Wen's wife, Li Ying's wife, Xiang Qi's wife, A Luzhen, Sahe Nian's wife, Xu Gu's wife, Feng Miaozhen, Lady Pucha, Lady Wugulun, Su Lan's wife, Mang Ge's wife, Lady Yin, Lady Bai, Nie the Filial Daughter, Zhongde's wife, Lady Li of Baofu, and Zhang Fengnu

sentences.zh: 漢成帝時，劉向始述三代賢妃淑女，及淫泆奢僭、興亡盛衰之所由，匯分類別，號《列女傳》，因以諷諫。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Cheng of Han, Liu Xiang first narrated the worthy consorts and virtuous women of the Three Dynasties, and the causes of debauchery, extravagance, overstepping of rank, and the rise and fall, flourishing and decline [of states]; he gathered and classified them, titled the work Biographies of Exemplary Women, and used it for admonition and remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Cheng of Han, Liu Xiang first set down the worthy consorts and virtuous ladies of the three ancient dynasties, together with the causes of licentiousness, extravagance, presumption, and the rise and fall of kingdoms; he sorted these accounts by category into a work called Biographies of Exemplary Women, using it to admonish the throne.

sentences.zh: 范曄始載之漢史。

translations.literal: Fan Ye first included it in the History of Han.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Ye was the first to carry such material in the History of the Later Han.

sentences.zh: 古者女子生十年有女師，漸長，有麻枲絲繭之事，有祭祀助奠之事；

translations.literal: In antiquity, when a girl had lived ten years she had a female teacher; as she gradually grew, she had hemp, ramie, silk, and cocoon work, and duties to assist in sacrifices and libations;
translations.idiomatic: In old times a girl of ten was given a woman's tutor; as she grew she learned hemp and silk work and how to help at sacrifices;

sentences.zh: 既嫁，職在中饋而已，故以無非無儀為賢。

translations.literal: Once married, her duty was only in the inner kitchen, and thus to be without fault and without unseemly conduct was deemed worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Once married, her sphere was the household kitchen alone; virtue meant simply doing nothing wrong and nothing unseemly.

sentences.zh: 若乃嫠居寡處，患難顛沛，是皆婦人之不幸也。

translations.literal: As for widowhood and living alone, hardship and destitution — all these are a woman's misfortune.
translations.idiomatic: Widowhood, solitude, hardship, and ruin were all counted a woman's misfortunes.

sentences.zh: 一遇不幸，卓然能自樹立，有烈丈夫之風，是以君子異之。

translations.literal: When they met with misfortune yet could stand forth resolutely on their own, with the spirit of a stern great man, for this reason gentlemen regarded them as extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when misfortune came, some women stood out on their own with a fierce, manly resolve — and for that gentlemen held them in special esteem.

sentences.zh: 阿鄰妻

translations.literal: The Wife of A Lin
translations.idiomatic: The Wife of A Lin

sentences.zh: 阿鄰妻沙裏質者，金源郡王銀術可之妹。

translations.literal: The wife of A Lin was Sharizhi, younger sister of Yinishu Ke, Prince of Jinyuan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: A Lin's wife Sharizhi was the younger sister of Yinishu Ke, Prince of Jinyuan.

sentences.zh: 天輔六年，黃龍府叛卒攻鈔旁近部族。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tianfu, mutinous soldiers of Huanglong Prefecture attacked and plundered nearby tribes.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Tianfu (1122), mutineers from Huanglong Prefecture raided neighboring clans.

sentences.zh: 是時，阿鄰從軍，沙裏質糾集附近居民得男女五百人，樹營柵為保守計。

translations.literal: At that time A Lin was with the army; Sharizhi gathered nearby inhabitants, men and women five hundred in number, and set up palisades as a plan for defense.
translations.idiomatic: A Lin was away on campaign; Sharizhi rallied five hundred men and women from the neighborhood, threw up a stockade, and prepared to hold out.

sentences.zh: 賊千余來攻，沙裏質以氈為甲，以裳為旗，男夫授甲，婦女鼓噪，沙裏質仗劍督戰，凡三日賊去。

translations.literal: More than a thousand bandits came to attack; Sharizhi used felt for armor and skirts for banners; men were given armor, women raised a clamor; Sharizhi wielded a sword to oversee the battle; in all three days the bandits departed.
translations.idiomatic: When more than a thousand rebels attacked, she improvised armor from felt and banners from skirts, armed the men, set the women to shouting, and herself took sword in hand to direct the fight; after three days the enemy withdrew.

sentences.zh: 皇統二年，論功封金源郡夫人。

translations.literal: In the second year of Huangtong, merit was assessed and she was enfeoffed as Lady of Jinyuan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Huangtong (1142), her service was rewarded with the title Lady of Jinyuan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 大定間，以其孫藥師為謀克。

translations.literal: In the Dading era her grandson Yaoshi was made a mouke.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dading reign (1161–1189), her grandson Yaoshi was appointed a company commander (mouke).

sentences.zh: 李寶信妻

translations.literal: The Wife of Li Baoxin
translations.idiomatic: The Wife of Li Baoxin

sentences.zh: 李寶信妻王氏。

translations.literal: The wife of Li Baoxin was the Wang clan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Baoxin's wife was surnamed Wang.

sentences.zh: 寶信為義豐縣令，張覺以平州叛，王氏陷賊中。

translations.literal: Baoxin was magistrate of Yifeng County; Zhang Jue rebelled with Ping Prefecture, and Lady Wang fell into the hands of the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Baoxin was magistrate of Yifeng County. When Zhang Jue rebelled at Pingzhou, Lady Wang was taken by the rebels.

sentences.zh: 賊欲逼室之，王氏罵賊，賊怒遂支解之。

translations.literal: The rebels wished to force her into the bedchamber; Lady Wang cursed the rebels, and in anger they dismembered her.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels tried to take her by force; she cursed them, and in their fury they cut her limb from limb.

sentences.zh: 大定十二年，贈「貞烈縣君」。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Dading she was posthumously granted the title "Chaste and Fierce District Lady."
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Dading (1172) she was posthumously honored as Chaste and Fierce District Lady.

sentences.zh: 韓慶民妻

translations.literal: The Wife of Han Qingmin
translations.idiomatic: The Wife of Han Qingmin

sentences.zh: 韓慶民妻者，不知何許人，亦不知其姓氏。

translations.literal: As for the wife of Han Qingmin, it is not known where she was from, nor is her surname known.
translations.idiomatic: Han Qingmin's wife — neither her birthplace nor her surname is recorded.

sentences.zh: 慶民事遼為宜州節度使。

translations.literal: Qingmin served the Liao as military governor of Yi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Qingmin had served the Liao as military governor of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 天會中，攻破宜州，慶民不屈而死，以其妻配將士，其妻誓死不從，遂自殺。

translations.literal: In the Tianhui era Yizhou was taken; Qingmin died rather than submit; his wife was given to the officers and soldiers; she vowed to die rather than obey and then killed herself.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianhui era (1123–1137) the Jin took Yizhou; Qingmin refused to yield and was put to death, and his wife was allotted to the troops. She swore she would not submit and took her own life.

sentences.zh: 世宗讀《太宗實錄》，見慶民夫婦事，歎曰：「如此節操，可謂難矣。」

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong, reading the Veritable Records of Taizong, saw the affair of Qingmin and his wife and sighed, saying, "Such constancy is truly hard to achieve."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong read the Veritable Records of Taizong and came upon the story of the couple, he sighed and said, "Constancy like that is rare indeed."

sentences.zh: 雷婦師氏

translations.literal: Mrs. Shi of the Lei Family
translations.idiomatic: Mrs. Shi of the Lei Family

sentences.zh: 雷婦師氏，夫亡，孝養舅姑。

translations.literal: Mrs. Shi of the Lei family — her husband died; she filially supported her parents-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: After her husband died, Mrs. Shi of the Lei household dutifully cared for her parents-in-law.

sentences.zh: 姑病，刲臂肉飼之，姑即愈。

translations.literal: Her mother-in-law fell ill; she cut flesh from her arm to feed her, and her mother-in-law was immediately cured.
translations.idiomatic: When her mother-in-law fell ill, she cut flesh from her own arm to feed her, and the elder woman recovered at once.

sentences.zh: 舅姑既歿。

translations.literal: When her parents-in-law had both died.
translations.idiomatic: After both parents-in-law had died,

sentences.zh: 兄師逵與夫侄規其財產，乃偽立謀證致之官，欲必嫁之。

translations.literal: Her elder brother Shi Kui and her husband's nephew plotted for her property; they falsely set up evidence and brought her before the magistrate, wishing to force her to remarry.
translations.idiomatic: her brother Shi Kui and her husband's nephew coveted her estate; they forged evidence and hauled her before the magistrate, intent on forcing her to marry again.

sentences.zh: 縣官不能辨曲直，師氏畏逼，乃投縣署井中死。

translations.literal: The county magistrate could not distinguish right from wrong; Lady Shi, fearing coercion, threw herself into the well at the county office and died.
translations.idiomatic: The magistrate could not tell right from wrong; terrified by the pressure, Lady Shi threw herself into the well at the county yamen and died.

sentences.zh: 詔有司祭其墓，賜諡曰「節」。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the authorities to sacrifice at her tomb and granted the posthumous title "Chaste."
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered officials to offer sacrifice at her tomb and gave her the posthumous name Chaste.

sentences.zh: 康住住

translations.literal: Kang Zhuzhu
translations.idiomatic: Kang Zhuzhu

sentences.zh: 康住住，鄜州人。

translations.literal: Kang Zhuzhu was a native of Fu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Zhuzhu was from Fu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 夫早亡，服闋，父取之歸家，許嚴沂為妻。

translations.literal: Her husband died early; when mourning was completed, her father took her back home and betrothed her to Yan Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Her husband died young; when her mourning ended, her father brought her home and promised her to Yan Yi.

sentences.zh: 康氏誓死弗聽，欲還夫家不可得，乃投崖而死。

translations.literal: Lady Kang vowed to die rather than obey; wishing to return to her husband's family but unable to do so, she cast herself from a cliff and died.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Kang swore she would die before she would listen; unable to return to her husband's house, she leapt from a cliff to her death.

sentences.zh: 詔有司致祭其墓。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the authorities to offer sacrifice at her tomb.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered officials to sacrifice at her tomb.

sentences.zh: 李文妻

translations.literal: The Wife of Li Wen
translations.idiomatic: The Wife of Li Wen

sentences.zh: 李文妻史氏，同州白水人。

translations.literal: The wife of Li Wen was the Shi clan, a native of Baishui in Tong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Wen's wife, née Shi, was from Baishui in Tong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 夫亡，服闋，誓死弗嫁。

translations.literal: Her husband died; when mourning was completed, she vowed to die rather than remarry.
translations.idiomatic: After her husband died and her mourning ended, she swore she would never marry again, even at the cost of her life.

sentences.zh: 父強取之歸，許邑人姚乙為妻。

translations.literal: Her father forcibly took her back and betrothed her to Yao Yi, a man of the district.
translations.idiomatic: Her father took her back by force and betrothed her to a local man named Yao Yi.

sentences.zh: 史氏不聽，姚訴之官，被逮，遂自縊死。

translations.literal: Lady Shi would not obey; Yao appealed to the authorities; she was arrested and then hanged herself.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Shi refused; Yao took the matter to court; when she was seized, she hanged herself.

sentences.zh: 詔有司致祭其墓。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the authorities to offer sacrifice at her tomb.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered officials to sacrifice at her tomb.

sentences.zh: 李英妻

translations.literal: The Wife of Li Ying
translations.idiomatic: The Wife of Li Ying

sentences.zh: 李英妻張氏。

translations.literal: The wife of Li Ying was the Zhang clan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ying's wife was surnamed Zhang.

sentences.zh: 英初為監察禦史，在中都，張居濰州。

translations.literal: Ying was at first a supervising censor at the Central Capital; Zhang resided at Wei Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Ying first served as a supervising censor at the Central Capital while Zhang remained at Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 貞祐元年冬，大元兵取濰州，入其家，張氏盡以所有財物與之。

translations.literal: In the winter of the first year of Zhenyou, the Great Yuan army took Wei Prefecture, entered her house, and Lady Zhang gave them all her possessions.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the first year of Zhenyou (1213), Mongol forces took Weizhou and entered her home; Lady Zhang gave them everything she owned.

sentences.zh: 既而，令張氏上馬，張曰：「我盡以物與汝，猶不見贖邪？

translations.literal: Then they ordered Lady Zhang to mount a horse. Zhang said, "I have given you all my goods — do you still not consider me redeemed?
translations.idiomatic: Then they ordered her onto a horse. Zhang said, "I have given you everything I own — is that still not enough to let me go?

sentences.zh: 」答曰「汝品官妻，當複為夫人。

translations.literal: " They answered, "You are the wife of a ranked official — you shall again become a lady."
translations.idiomatic: " They replied, "You are a ranked official's wife — you will be a lady again."

sentences.zh: 」張曰：「我死則為李氏鬼。

translations.literal: " Zhang said, "If I die I shall be a ghost of the Li family."
translations.idiomatic: " Zhang said, "In death I shall be a ghost of the Li household alone."

sentences.zh: 頓坐不起，遂見殺。

translations.literal: She sat down at once and would not rise, and was then killed.
translations.idiomatic: She sat down and would not budge, and they killed her.

sentences.zh: 追封隴西郡夫人，諡「莊潔」。

translations.literal: She was posthumously enfeoffed as Lady of Longxi Commandery, with the posthumous title "Solemn and Pure."
translations.idiomatic: She was posthumously made Lady of Longxi Commandery, with the posthumous name Solemn and Pure.

sentences.zh: 英仕至御史中丞，有傳。

translations.literal: Ying rose to Vice Censor-in-Chief; he has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: Ying rose to vice censor-in-chief; he has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 相琪妻

translations.literal: The Wife of Xiang Qi
translations.idiomatic: The Wife of Xiang Qi

sentences.zh: 相琪妻欒氏，有姿色。

translations.literal: The wife of Xiang Qi was the Luan clan, possessed of beauty.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Qi's wife, née Luan, was a woman of striking beauty.

sentences.zh: 琪為萊州掖縣司吏。

translations.literal: Qi was a clerk of Ye County in Laizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Qi was a clerk in Ye County, Laizhou.

sentences.zh: 貞祐三年八月，紅祆賊陷掖縣，琪與欒氏及子俱為所得。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the third year of Zhenyou, Red Turban bandits took Ye County; Qi, Lady Luan, and their son were all captured.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the third year of Zhenyou (1215), Red Turban rebels overran Ye County; Qi, Lady Luan, and their son were all taken.

sentences.zh: 賊見欒悅之，殺琪及其子而誘欒。

translations.literal: The bandits, pleased at the sight of Luan, killed Qi and his son and tried to entice Luan.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels, taken with Luan's looks, killed Qi and their son and tried to win her over.

sentences.zh: 欒奮起以頭觸賊而僕，罵曰：「我豈為犬彘所汙者哉。

translations.literal: Luan sprang up, struck the bandit with her head and knocked him down, and cursed, saying, "How could I be defiled by dogs and swine!
translations.idiomatic: Luan leapt up, butted a rebel to the ground, and cried, "Would I let dogs and pigs defile me?

sentences.zh: 」賊怒，殺之。

translations.literal: " The bandits in anger killed her.
translations.idiomatic: " In their rage they killed her.

sentences.zh: 追封西河縣君，諡「莊潔」。

translations.literal: She was posthumously enfeoffed as District Lady of Xihe, with the posthumous title "Solemn and Pure."
translations.idiomatic: She was posthumously made District Lady of Xihe, with the posthumous name Solemn and Pure.

sentences.zh: 阿魯真

translations.literal: A Luzhen
translations.idiomatic: A Luzhen

sentences.zh: 撒合輦妻

translations.literal: The Wife of Sahe Nian
translations.idiomatic: The Wife of Sahe Nian

sentences.zh: 獨吉氏，平章政事千家奴之女，護衛銀術可妹也。

translations.literal: The Duji clan — daughter of Qianjianu, Grand Councilor of the Secretariat, and younger sister of Yinishu Ke of the Imperial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Duji was the daughter of Grand Councilor Qianjianu and the younger sister of Guardsman Yinishu Ke.

sentences.zh: 自幼動有禮法，及適內族撒合輦。

translations.literal: From childhood her conduct observed ritual propriety; when she married Sahe Nian of the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: From girlhood she was noted for propriety; she married Sahe Nian of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 閨門肅如。

translations.literal: The inner quarters were solemn and orderly.
translations.idiomatic: Their household was grave and orderly.

sentences.zh: 撒合輦為中京留守，大兵圍之，撒合輦疽發背不能軍，獨吉氏度城必破，謂撒合輦曰：「公本無功能，徒以宗室故嘗在禁近，以至提點近侍局，同判睦親府，今又為留守外路第一等官，受國家恩最厚。

translations.literal: Sahe Nian was defender of the Central Capital; the great army besieged it; Sahe Nian had a carbuncle on his back and could not command the troops; Lady Duji judged that the city would surely fall, and said to Sahe Nian, "You originally had no ability; only because you were of the imperial clan were you once near the forbidden precinct, rising to oversee the Bureau of Palace Attendants and associate judge of the Office of Imperial Kin, and now again you are defender — the foremost official on the outer circuits — receiving the state's favor most heavily."
translations.idiomatic: Sahe Nian was defender of the Central Capital when a great army laid siege. A carbuncle on his back kept him from taking the field. Lady Duji saw the city was doomed and told him, "You never had real talent — you rose only because you are of the imperial clan, from posts at court to overseer of the Palace Attendants and associate judge of the Office of Imperial Kin, and now defender, the highest post on the frontier. The state has heaped favor on you."

sentences.zh: 今大兵臨城，公不幸病，不能戰禦，設若城破，公當率精銳奪門而出，攜一子走京師。

translations.literal: Now the great army is at the walls; you are unfortunately ill and cannot fight in defense; if the city should fall, you ought to lead picked troops, break out through the gate, take one son, and flee to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Now the enemy is at the walls and you are too ill to fight. If the city falls, lead your best men, break out, take one son, and ride for the capital.

sentences.zh: 不能則獨赴京師，又不能，戰而死猶可報國，幸無以我為慮。

translations.literal: If you cannot, then go alone to the capital; if you cannot do that either, to die fighting would still repay the state — only do not worry on my account.
translations.idiomatic: If you cannot manage that, go alone to the capital; if you cannot even do that, die fighting and you will still have served the state. Do not spare a thought for me.

sentences.zh: 」撒合輦出巡城，獨吉氏乃取平日衣服妝具玩好布之臥榻，資貨悉散之家人，豔妝盛服過於平日，且戒女使曰：「我死則扶置榻上，以衾覆面，四圍舉火焚之。

translations.literal: " Sahe Nian went out to inspect the walls; Lady Duji then took her usual clothes, toilet articles, and cherished objects and spread them on the couch, distributed all valuables to the household, dressed in splendid makeup and fine garments more lavish than on ordinary days, and moreover instructed the maids, saying, "When I die, support me and lay me on the couch, cover my face with a quilt, and set fire all around to burn me."
translations.idiomatic: " While Sahe Nian went out to inspect the walls, Lady Duji spread her everyday clothes, cosmetics, and treasures on the bed, gave her valuables to the household, and dressed more richly than ever. She told her maids, "When I am dead, lay me on the couch, cover my face with a quilt, and burn me all around."

sentences.zh: 無使兵見吾面。

translations.literal: Do not let the soldiers see my face.
translations.idiomatic: Let no soldier see my face."

sentences.zh: 」言訖，閉門自經而死。

translations.literal: " When she had finished speaking, she shut the door and hanged herself.
translations.idiomatic: When she had said this, she shut the door and hanged herself.

sentences.zh: 家人如言，臥屍榻上，以衾覆之。

translations.literal: The household did as she had said, laid the corpse on the couch, and covered it with a quilt.
translations.idiomatic: The household did as she had said and laid her body on the couch under a quilt.

sentences.zh: 撒合輦從外室，家人告以夫人之死，撒合輦拊榻曰：「夫人不辱我，我肯辱朝廷乎！

translations.literal: Sahe Nian came from the outer room; the household told him of his lady's death; Sahe Nian struck the couch and said, "My lady did not disgrace me — would I disgrace the court!
translations.idiomatic: Sahe Nian returned from outside; the household told him his wife was dead. He struck the couch and cried, "She did not shame me — would I shame the court?

sentences.zh: 」因命焚之。

translations.literal: " He then ordered her burned.
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered the fire lit.

sentences.zh: 年三十有六。

translations.literal: She was thirty-six years of age.
translations.idiomatic: She was thirty-six.

sentences.zh: 少頃，城破，撒合輦率死士欲奪門出，不果，投壕水死，有傳。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward the city fell; Sahe Nian led death-defying troops wishing to seize the gate and break out, but did not succeed, and cast himself into the moat and died; he has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the city fell. Sahe Nian led his best men in a dash for the gate but failed, threw himself into the moat, and drowned; he has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 許古妻

translations.literal: The Wife of Xu Gu
translations.idiomatic: The Wife of Xu Gu

sentences.zh: 許古妻劉氏，定海軍節度使仲洙之女也。

translations.literal: The wife of Xu Gu was the Liu clan, daughter of Zhongzhu, military governor of the Dinghai Army.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Gu's wife, née Liu, was the daughter of Zhongzhu, military governor of the Dinghai Army.

sentences.zh: 貞祐初，古挈家僑居蒲城，從留劉氏母子于蒲，仕於朝。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenyou, Gu took his family to live as sojourners at Pucheng, leaving Lady Liu and her children at Pu while he took office at court.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenyou, Gu moved his family to lodge at Pucheng, left Lady Liu and the children at Pu, and took office at court.

sentences.zh: 既而，兵圍蒲，劉謂二女曰：「汝父在朝，而兵勢如此，事不可保。

translations.literal: Before long troops besieged Pu; Liu said to her two daughters, "Your father is at court, yet the military situation is such — affairs cannot be assured."
translations.idiomatic: Before long troops besieged Pu. Liu said to her two daughters, "Your father is at court, and with the army pressing like this, nothing is safe."

sentences.zh: 若城破被驅，一為所汙奈何？

translations.literal: If the city falls and we are driven off, how could we bear to be defiled even once?
translations.idiomatic: If the city falls and we are driven away, how could we endure being defiled?

sentences.zh: 不若俱死以自全。

translations.literal: Better to die together and preserve our integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Better that we all die and keep ourselves whole."

sentences.zh: 」已而，攻城益急，於是劉氏與二女相繼自盡。

translations.literal: " Before long the assault grew fiercer; thereupon Lady Liu and her two daughters killed themselves in succession.
translations.idiomatic: The assault grew fiercer, and Lady Liu and her two daughters took their lives one after another.

sentences.zh: 有司以聞於朝，四年五月，追封劉氏為郡君，諡曰「貞潔」，其長女諡曰「定薑」，次「肅薑」，以其事付史館。

translations.literal: The authorities reported to the court; in the fifth month of the fourth year she was posthumously enfeoffed as District Lady, with the posthumous title "Chaste and Pure"; her elder daughter was given the posthumous title "Dingjiang," the younger "Sujiang"; the affair was entrusted to the Historiography Institute.
translations.idiomatic: Officials reported the matter to court; in the fifth month of the fourth year Lady Liu was posthumously made a district lady with the name Chaste and Pure, her elder daughter Dingjiang and the younger Sujiang; the Historiography Institute was ordered to record the affair.

sentences.zh: 馮妙真

translations.literal: Feng Miaozhen
translations.idiomatic: Feng Miaozhen

sentences.zh: 馮妙真，刑部尚書延登之女也。

translations.literal: Feng Miaozhen was the daughter of Yandeng, Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Miaozhen was the daughter of Yandeng, Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 生十有八年，適進士張綎。

translations.literal: At the age of eighteen she married the jinshi Zhang Chao.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen she married the jinshi Zhang Chao.

sentences.zh: 興定五年，綎為洛川主簿。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xingding, Chao was chief clerk of Luochuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Xingding (1221), Chao was chief clerk of Luochuan.

sentences.zh: 大元兵破葭州、綏德，遂入鄜延。

translations.literal: The Great Yuan army took Jia Prefecture and Suide, then entered Fuyan.
translations.idiomatic: Mongol forces took Jiazhou and Suide and pushed into the Fuyan region.

sentences.zh: 鄜人震恐具守備，守臣以西路輸芻粟不時至，檄慥詣平涼督之。

translations.literal: The people of Fu were alarmed and made full preparations for defense; the defending official, because fodder and grain from the western route did not arrive on time, issued an order for Chao to go to Pingliang to supervise it.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Fu were terrified and threw up defenses; because fodder and grain from the west were late, the defender ordered Chao to Pingliang to hurry the supply.

sentences.zh: 時延登為平涼行省員外郎，綎欲偕妙真以往，妙真辭曰：「舅姑老矣。

translations.literal: At that time Yandeng was assistant commissioner of the Pingliang Branch Secretariat; Chao wished to take Miaozhen with him; Miaozhen declined, saying, "My parents-in-law are old.
translations.idiomatic: Yandeng was then assistant commissioner at the Pingliang secretariat; Chao wanted Miaozhen to go with him, but she refused: "My parents-in-law are old.

sentences.zh: 雖有叔姒，妾能安乎。

translations.literal: Although there is an aunt by marriage, how could your handmaid be at ease?
translations.idiomatic: Though my husband's aunt is here, how could I be easy in my mind?

sentences.zh: 子行，妾留奉養。

translations.literal: You go; your handmaid will remain to serve and support them."
translations.idiomatic: You go; I will stay to care for them."

sentences.zh: 」十一月，洛川破，妙真從舅姑匿窟室，兵索得之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Luochuan fell; Miaozhen followed her parents-in-law into hiding in a cave-room; the soldiers searched and found them.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Luochuan fell. Miaozhen hid with her parents-in-law in a cave; soldiers found them.

sentences.zh: 妙真泣與舅姑訣曰：「婦生不辰，不得終執箕帚，義不從辱。

translations.literal: Miaozhen wept and took leave of her parents-in-law, saying, "This wife was born at an unlucky hour and cannot to the end wield broom and dustpan; by right I will not submit to disgrace."
translations.idiomatic: Miaozhen wept her farewell: "I was born under an ill star and cannot serve you to the end; I will not live in disgrace."

sentences.zh: 」即攜三子赴井死。

translations.literal: " She then took her three sons and went to a well and died.
translations.idiomatic: She took her three sons and threw herself into a well.

sentences.zh: 縣人從而死者數十人。

translations.literal: Several tens of people in the county followed her in death.
translations.idiomatic: Several dozen people in the county followed her example and died.

sentences.zh: 明年春，綎發井得屍，殯於縣之東郭外。

translations.literal: The next spring Chao had the well opened and obtained the corpses, and buried them outside the eastern suburb of the county.
translations.idiomatic: The next spring Chao had the well opened, recovered the bodies, and buried them outside the eastern gate of the county seat.

sentences.zh: 死時年二十四。

translations.literal: At death she was twenty-four years of age.
translations.idiomatic: She was twenty-four when she died.

sentences.zh: 蒲察氏

translations.literal: The Pucha Clan
translations.idiomatic: Lady Pucha

sentences.zh: 蒲察氏，字明秀，鄜州帥訥申之女，完顏長樂之妻也。

translations.literal: The Pucha clan — her style name was Mingsiu; daughter of Neshen, commander of Fu Prefecture; wife of Wanyan Changle.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Pucha, styled Mingsiu, was the daughter of Fu Prefecture commander Neshen and the wife of Wanyan Changle.

sentences.zh: 哀宗遷歸德，以長樂為總領，將兵扈從。

translations.literal: Emperor Aizong moved to Guide; Changle was made chief commander and led troops in escort.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Aizong moved the court to Guide, Changle was made chief commander and marched with an escort.

sentences.zh: 將行，屬蒲察氏曰：「無他言，夫人慎毋辱此身。

translations.literal: As he was about to depart, he charged Lady Pucha, saying, "Say nothing else — my lady, take care not to disgrace this person."
translations.idiomatic: Before he left, he told Lady Pucha, "I have only this to say: do not let yourself be dishonored."

sentences.zh: 」明秀曰：「君第致身事上，無以妾為念。

translations.literal: " Mingsiu said, "You need only devote your person to serving the sovereign; do not think of your handmaid."
translations.idiomatic: " Mingsiu replied, "Give yourself wholly to the throne; do not worry about me."

sentences.zh: 妾必不辱。

translations.literal: Your handmaid will surely not be disgraced.
translations.idiomatic: I will not bring shame on us."

sentences.zh: 」長樂一子在幼，出妻柴氏所生也，明秀撫育如己出。

translations.literal: " Changle had one son still young, born of his divorced wife the Chai clan; Mingsiu reared him as if he were her own.
translations.idiomatic: Changle had a young son by his former wife, Lady Chai; Mingsiu raised him as her own.

sentences.zh: 崔立之變，驅從官妻子于省中，人自閱之。

translations.literal: At the upheaval of Cui Li, the wives and children of attendant officials were driven into the provincial offices, each man to examine and choose among them.
translations.idiomatic: During Cui Li's coup, officials' wives and children were herded into the provincial compound for the men to pick over.

sentences.zh: 蒲察氏聞，以幼子付婢僕，且與之金幣，親具衣棺祭物，與家人訣曰：「崔立不道，強人妻女，兵在城下，吾何所逃，惟一死不負吾夫耳。

translations.literal: When Lady Pucha heard, she entrusted the young son to maids and servants, gave them gold and coins, personally prepared clothes, coffin, and sacrificial goods, and took leave of her household, saying, "Cui Li is without the Way, forcibly taking men's wives and daughters; with troops below the walls, where could I flee? Only death can keep me from failing my husband."
translations.idiomatic: When Lady Pucha heard, she gave her young son to the servants with gold and coins, prepared her own burial clothes and offerings, and said farewell: "Cui Li is a villain who seizes men's wives and daughters; the enemy is at the walls and I have nowhere to run — only death can keep me true to my husband."

sentences.zh: 汝等惟善養幼子。

translations.literal: You need only rear the young son well."
translations.idiomatic: See to it that you raise the boy well."

sentences.zh: 」遂自縊而死，欣然若不以死為難者。

translations.literal: " She then hanged herself, as gladly as if she did not regard death as difficult.
translations.idiomatic: She hanged herself, serene as if death were nothing hard.

sentences.zh: 時年二十七。

translations.literal: At the time she was twenty-seven years of age.
translations.idiomatic: She was twenty-seven.

sentences.zh: 烏古論氏

translations.literal: The Wugulun Clan
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wugulun

sentences.zh: 烏古論氏，伯祥之妹，臨洮總管陀滿胡土門之妻也。

translations.literal: The Wugulun clan — younger sister of Boxiang; wife of Tuoman Hutumen, commander-general of Lintao.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wugulun was the younger sister of Boxiang and the wife of Tuoman Hutumen, commander-general of Lintao.

sentences.zh: 伯祥朝貴中聲譽藉甚，胡土門死王事。

translations.literal: Boxiang's reputation among the court nobility was very great; Hutumen died in service to the state.
translations.idiomatic: Boxiang was greatly esteemed among the court elite; Hutumen died in the state's service.

sentences.zh: 崔立之變，衣冠家婦女多為所汙，烏古論氏謂家人曰：「吾夫不辱朝廷，我敢辱吾兄及吾夫乎。

translations.literal: At the upheaval of Cui Li, many women of gentry families were defiled; Lady Wugulun said to her household, "My husband did not disgrace the court — how dare I disgrace my brother and my husband?
translations.idiomatic: During Cui Li's coup many ladies of good families were violated. Lady Wugulun told her household, "My husband did not shame the court — how could I shame my brother and my husband?

sentences.zh: 」即自縊。

translations.literal: " She then hanged herself.
translations.idiomatic: " She hanged herself at once.

sentences.zh: 一婢從死。

translations.literal: One maid followed her in death.
translations.idiomatic: One maid died with her.

sentences.zh: 素蘭妻

translations.literal: The Wife of Su Lan
translations.idiomatic: The Wife of Su Lan

sentences.zh: 參政完顏素蘭妻，亡其姓氏。

translations.literal: The wife of Grand Councilor Wanyan Sulan — her surname is lost.
translations.idiomatic: The wife of Grand Councilor Wanyan Sulan — her surname is not recorded.

sentences.zh: 當崔立之變，謂所親曰：「吾夫有天下重名，吾豈肯隨眾陷身以辱吾夫乎。

translations.literal: At the upheaval of Cui Li, she said to those close to her, "My husband bears a weighty name throughout the realm — how could I be willing to follow the crowd into ruin and disgrace my husband?
translations.idiomatic: When Cui Li's coup came, she told her intimates, "My husband's name stands high in the realm — would I follow the crowd into disgrace and shame him?

sentences.zh: 今日一死固當，但不可無名而死，亦不可離吾家而死。

translations.literal: To die today is surely fitting, but one must not die without a name, nor die away from my household."
translations.idiomatic: Death today is only right — but I will not die without honor, and I will not die outside my own house."

sentences.zh: 」即自縊於室。

translations.literal: " She then hanged herself in her chamber.
translations.idiomatic: She hanged herself in her room.

sentences.zh: 忙哥妻

translations.literal: The Wife of Mang Ge
translations.idiomatic: The Wife of Mang Ge

sentences.zh: 溫特罕氏，夫完顏忙哥，五朵山宣差提控回裏不之子也，系出蕭王。

translations.literal: The Wentehan clan — her husband was Wanyan Mang Ge, son of Huilibu, commissioner and commander of Wuduoshan, descended from Prince Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wentehan's husband was Wanyan Mang Ge, son of Huilibu, commissioner at Wuduoshan — a descendant of Prince Xiao.

sentences.zh: 忙哥叔父益都，節度秦州，為大元兵所攻，適病不能軍，忙哥為提控，獨當一面。

translations.literal: Mang Ge's uncle Yidu was military governor of Qin Prefecture; attacked by the Great Yuan army, he happened to be ill and could not command the troops; Mang Ge as commander alone held one front.
translations.idiomatic: Mang Ge's uncle Yidu was military governor of Qinzhou; when Mongol forces attacked, Yidu fell ill and could not take the field, and Mang Ge alone held the line as commander.

sentences.zh: 兵退而益都死，忙哥以城守功世襲謀克，收充奉禦。

translations.literal: The army withdrew and Yidu died; Mang Ge for his merit in defending the city inherited the post of mouke and was enrolled as a palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: After the enemy withdrew Yidu died; for defending the city Mang Ge inherited a company command (mouke) and was enrolled as a palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 及崔立之變，忙哥義不受辱，與其妻訣。

translations.literal: When the upheaval of Cui Li came, Mang Ge by right would not accept disgrace, and took leave of his wife.
translations.idiomatic: When Cui Li's coup came, Mang Ge refused to live in dishonor and said farewell to his wife.

sentences.zh: 妻曰：「君能為國家死，我不能為君死乎。

translations.literal: His wife said, "You can die for the state — can I not die for you?
translations.idiomatic: His wife said, "You can die for the state — cannot I die for you?

sentences.zh: 」一婢曰：「主死，婢將安歸。

translations.literal: " One maid said, "When the master dies, whither shall the maid return?
translations.idiomatic: " A maid said, "When my master dies, where shall I go?

sentences.zh: 」是日，夫婦以一繩同縊，婢從之。

translations.literal: " That day husband and wife hanged themselves on one rope; the maid followed them.
translations.idiomatic: That day husband and wife hanged themselves from one rope; the maid followed.

sentences.zh: 尹氏，完顏豬兒之妻也。

translations.literal: The Yin clan — wife of Wanyan Zhuer.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Yin was the wife of Wanyan Zhuer.

sentences.zh: 豬兒系出蕭王，天興二年正月從哀宗為南面元帥，戰死黃陵岡。

translations.literal: Zhuer was descended from Prince Xiao; in the first month of the second year of Tianxing he followed Emperor Aizong as southern-route commander-in-chief and died in battle at Huangling Mound.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuer was of Prince Xiao's line; in the first month of the second year of Tianxing (1233) he followed Emperor Aizong as southern-route commander-in-chief and was killed at Huangling Mound.

sentences.zh: 其妻金源郡夫人聞豬兒死，聚家資焚之，遂自縊，年三十一。

translations.literal: His wife, Lady of Jinyuan Commandery, on hearing of Zhuer's death gathered the family wealth and burned it, then hanged herself; she was thirty-one years of age.
translations.idiomatic: His wife, Lady of Jinyuan Commandery, heard of his death, burned the family possessions, and hanged herself; she was thirty-one.

sentences.zh: 豬兒贈官，弟長住即日詔補護衛。

translations.literal: Zhuer was granted posthumous office; his younger brother Changzhu was that same day ordered by edict to fill a guardsman's post.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuer was given posthumous rank; his younger brother Changzhu was appointed a guardsman the same day by edict.

sentences.zh: 聶孝女

translations.literal: Nie the Filial Daughter
translations.idiomatic: Nie the Filial Daughter

sentences.zh: 聶孝女，字舜英，尚書左右司員外郎天驥之長女也。

translations.literal: Nie the Filial Daughter — her style name was Shunying; eldest daughter of Tianji, assistant commissioner of the Left and Right Bureaus of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Nie the Filial Daughter, styled Shunying, was the eldest daughter of Tianji, assistant commissioner of the Secretariat's Left and Right Bureaus.

sentences.zh: 年二十三，適進士張伯豪。

translations.literal: At the age of twenty-three she married the jinshi Zhang Bohao.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty-three she married the jinshi Zhang Bohao.

sentences.zh: 伯豪卒，歸父母家。

translations.literal: Bohao died; she returned to her parents' home.
translations.idiomatic: When Bohao died she returned to her parents' home.

sentences.zh: 及哀宗遷歸德，天驥留汴。

translations.literal: When Emperor Aizong moved to Guide, Tianji remained at Bian.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Aizong moved to Guide, Tianji stayed behind at Bian (Kaifeng).

sentences.zh: 崔立劫殺宰相，天驥被創甚，日夜悲泣，恨不即死。

translations.literal: Cui Li seized and killed the chief councilor; Tianji was badly wounded and wept day and night, hating that he could not die at once.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Li seized and killed the chief councilor; Tianji was gravely wounded and wept day and night, wishing only to die.

sentences.zh: 舜英謁醫救療百方，至刲其股雜他肉以進，而天驥竟死。

translations.literal: Shunying sought physicians and tried every remedy; she even cut flesh from her thigh and mixed it with other meat to present to him, yet Tianji died in the end.
translations.idiomatic: Shunying sought every physician and remedy; she even cut flesh from her thigh and mixed it with other meat for him to eat, but Tianji died all the same.

sentences.zh: 時京城圍久食盡，閭巷間有嫁妻易一飽者，重以崔立之變，剽奪暴淩，無複人理。

translations.literal: At the time the capital had long been besieged and food was exhausted; in the lanes and alleys some sold their wives for a single full meal; added to the upheaval of Cui Li, plunder and violent oppression — human decency was no more.
translations.idiomatic: The capital had been besieged so long that food was gone; in the streets men sold their wives for a single meal; with Cui Li's coup came looting and violence until human decency itself seemed dead.

sentences.zh: 舜英頗讀書知義理，自以年尚少艾，夫既亡，父又死非命，比為兵所汙，何若從吾父于地下乎。

translations.literal: Shunying had read books and knew right principle; she considered that her years were still young, her husband already dead, her father had died an unnatural death — compared with being defiled by soldiers, how much better to follow my father in the underworld.
translations.idiomatic: Shunying was well read and understood duty; still young, with her husband dead and her father killed, she thought that to be violated by soldiers was worse than joining her father underground.

sentences.zh: 葬其父之明日，絕脰而死。

translations.literal: On the day after burying her father she severed her throat and died.
translations.idiomatic: The day after her father's burial she cut her throat and died.

sentences.zh: 一時士女賢之，有為泣下者。

translations.literal: Men and women of the time honored her; some wept.
translations.idiomatic: Men and women of the day held her in honor; some wept.

sentences.zh: 其家以舜英合葬張伯豪之墓。

translations.literal: Her family buried Shunying together with Zhang Bohao in one tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Her family buried her with Zhang Bohao in a shared grave.

sentences.zh: 仲德妻

translations.literal: The Wife of Zhongde
translations.idiomatic: The Wife of Zhongde

sentences.zh: 完顏仲德妻，不知其族氏。

translations.literal: The wife of Wanyan Zhongde — her clan and surname are not known.
translations.idiomatic: The wife of Wanyan Zhongde — her clan and surname are not recorded.

sentences.zh: 崔立之變，妻自毀其容服，攜妾及二子紿以采蔬，自汴走蔡。

translations.literal: At the upheaval of Cui Li, the wife disfigured her face and dress, took a concubine and two sons, pretended to be gathering vegetables, and fled from Bian to Cai.
translations.idiomatic: During Cui Li's coup she marred her face and clothes, took a concubine and her two sons, pretended to be gathering vegetables, and fled from Bian to Cai.

sentences.zh: 蔡被圍，丁男皆乘城拒守，謂仲德曰：「事勢若此，丈夫能為國出力，婦人獨不能耶！

translations.literal: Cai was besieged; all able-bodied men mounted the walls to resist; she said to Zhongde, "Affairs stand thus — a husband can exert strength for the state; can a woman alone not do so!
translations.idiomatic: When Cai was besieged and every able man was on the walls, she told Zhongde, "Matters stand as they do — if men can serve the state, cannot women as well?

sentences.zh: 」率諸命婦自作一軍，親運矢石於城下，城中婦女爭出繼之。

translations.literal: " She led the titled ladies to form an army of their own, personally hauling arrows and stones below the walls; women in the city vied to come out and follow.
translations.idiomatic: She rallied the noble wives into a corps of their own, hauled arrows and stones to the foot of the wall herself, and women throughout the city rushed out to join them.

sentences.zh: 城破自盡。

translations.literal: When the city fell she killed herself.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell she took her own life.

sentences.zh: 寶符李氏

translations.literal: Lady Li of Baofu
translations.idiomatic: Lady Li of Baofu

sentences.zh: 哀宗寶符李氏，國亡從後妃北遷，至宣德州，居摩訶院，日夕寢處佛殿中，作幡旆。

translations.literal: Emperor Aizong's Baofu, Lady Li — when the state perished she followed the empresses and consorts north; reaching Xuande Prefecture, she dwelt at the Mahā Monastery, day and night sleeping in the Buddha hall, making banners and pennants.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Aizong's consort Baofu, Lady Li, followed the imperial women north after the fall; at Xuande Prefecture she lived in the Mahā Monastery, slept in the Buddha hall, and spent her days making ritual banners.

sentences.zh: 會當赴龍庭，將發，即於佛像前自縊死，且自書門紙曰：「寶符禦侍此處身故。

translations.literal: When the time came to go to the Dragon Court and they were about to depart, she hanged herself before the Buddha image and moreover wrote on the door paper, "Baofu, imperial attendant, died here."
translations.idiomatic: When she was to be taken to the Mongol court and the party was about to leave, she hanged herself before the Buddha image and wrote on the door, "Baofu, imperial attendant, died here."

sentences.zh: 」後人至其處，見其遺跡，憐而哀之。

translations.literal: " Later people who came to the place, seeing her traces, pitied and mourned her.
translations.idiomatic: Those who came afterward, finding what she had left, pitied and mourned her.

sentences.zh: 張鳳奴

translations.literal: Zhang Fengnu
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fengnu

sentences.zh: 天興元年，北兵攻城，矢石之際忽見一女子呼於城下曰：「我倡女張鳳奴也，許州破被俘至此。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianxing, northern troops besieged the city; amid arrows and stones a woman was suddenly seen calling from below the wall, saying, "I am the singing-girl Zhang Fengnu; Xuzhou fell and I was captured and brought here.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianxing (1232), as northern troops besieged the city, a woman suddenly called from below the walls amid the arrows and stones: "I am the courtesan Zhang Fengnu; when Xuzhou fell I was taken and brought here.

sentences.zh: 彼軍不日去矣，諸君努力為國堅守，無為所欺也。

translations.literal: That army will before long depart; you gentlemen strive to hold firm for the state — do not be deceived."
translations.idiomatic: Their army will soon withdraw; hold the city for your country and do not be deceived."

sentences.zh: 」言竟，投濠而死。

translations.literal: " When she had finished speaking, she cast herself into the moat and died.
translations.idiomatic: When she had said this, she threw herself into the moat and died.

sentences.zh: 朝廷遣使馳祭於西門。

translations.literal: The court dispatched an envoy to offer swift sacrifice at the western gate.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent an envoy to offer sacrifice in haste at the western gate.

sentences.zh: 正大、天興之際，婦人節義可知者特數人耳。

translations.literal: In the Zhengda and Tianxing eras, women whose constancy and righteousness can be known were only a few in number.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhengda and Tianxing years, only a handful of women left records of such fidelity.

sentences.zh: 鳳奴之事別史錄之。

translations.literal: Fengnu's affair is recorded in a separate history.
translations.idiomatic: Fengnu's story is recorded elsewhere in the histories.

sentences.zh: 蓋亦有所激雲。

translations.literal: Presumably there was also something that stirred [such accounts].
translations.idiomatic: Surely something in the times stirred them to such acts.
